lines.text: Your agent sounds sure, but it doesn't know your project.
So you explain it again, every session, every tool.
What you wrote down is scattered, stale, and unverifiable.
Meet open knowledge. One knowledge base for your team and every agent.
Start with the docs you already have. One command turns plain markdown into a managed knowledge base. No docs yet? Your agent drafts them.
Search it, and every answer comes with receipts. The file, the lines, and a content hash. Your agent stops guessing and starts citing.
One wiki for every agent. Any MCP client can search it. Switch tools and keep your knowledge.
When things change, your agent proposes the edit. You review the diff, then save. The history lives in Git.
Checks catch stale knowledge before it ships. When a source changes, you know. And every pull request is tested before it merges.
Then ship knowledge like code. Every release is immutable, and rollback is one command.
One lifecycle. From a folder of notes to production. No migrations.
Open knowledge. Build a knowledge base your agents can use. Start today at openknowledge .sh.
